content.title: Boston Marathon weather forecast: Cool, windy and dry
content.text: The 2026 Boston Marathon on Monday, April 20, is forecasted to be chilly and breezy, with temperatures in the mid-30s to upper-40s°F (0 °C to 10 °C) and mostly dry conditions. A cold front will bring stiff 10–25 mph (16 to 40 KPH) northwesterly winds, potentially making it one of the coldest Boston Marathons on record.Key 2026 Race Day Conditions (April 20):Start Line (Hopkinton): Temperatures are expected to be in the upper 20s to mid-30s°F, feeling closer to 37°F () in some areas.Finish Line (Boston): Temperatures will rise to the mid-40s to low 50s°F by the afternoon.Wind: Winds will be a significant factor, blowing at 10-25 mph, which could create a brisk crosswind/tailwind for runners.Conditions: Mostly dry with partly sunny skies, although some, particularly those waiting to start, will experience very chilly conditions. Rain may begin at the end of the marathon for those who are in the final wave start. It will be a rainy afternoon and evening.Runner and spectator tips:For Runners: The cool, dry weather is beneficial for running fast times, though the wind will be strong. There may be a tailwind most of the way, therefore assisting.For Spectators: It will feel quite cold, especially with the wind; warm, layered clothing is advised.Start times: The 2026 Boston Marathon (130th running) starts in Hopkinton on April 20th, with wheelchair divisions beginning at 9:06 a.m. ET, followed by professional athletes at 9:37 a.m. Open division runners begin in six staggered waves from 10:00 a.m. to 11:21 a.m.2026 Boston Marathon Start Times (ET)9:06 a.m.: Men’s Wheelchair9:09 a.m.: Women’s Wheelchair9:30 a.m.: Handcycles & Duos9:37 a.m.: Professional Men9:47 a.m.:
